🚨🇲🇽 <u>Trump Says a Mexico Deal Is "Close," Then Demands Mexico Lose Its Surplus</u>

Back at the White House after meeting Sheinbaum at APEC, Trump said a trade deal with Mexico is close. Then he named his condition: "They have a huge surplus with the United States. I told her: 'Claudia, we can't allow a surplus.'" He also repeated that "the cartels control Mexico." A big share of that surplus is US-owned factories in Mexico shipping north. Sheinbaum's line since Shenzhen hasn't changed: talks are "very advanced," and the next meeting is at the G20 in December.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>At APEC, Sheinbaum Puts People Above Markets</u>

In Shenzhen, before the leaders of APEC's 21 economies, Sheinbaum argued that no nation's growth should be built on weakening others. "In Mexico, we believe development shouldn't be measured only by economic growth, the size of markets or technological leadership. It must be measured, even in the face of artificial intelligence, above all in people's lives." Her pitch to the Asia-Pacific was to cut inequality and cooperate instead of compete. She made it in the same week she sat down with both Xi and Trump.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>64.7% of Mexicans Are Time-Poor</u>

Same job, same eight hours, completely different lives. Writing in Contralínea, Ana María Ibarra Olguín lays out Mexico's "time poverty," the lack of enough hours to rest, look after yourself or have any leisure at all. As of 2024 it hit 64.7% of people nationwide; the capital's Evaluation Council puts Mexico City at 57.1%. The causes are structural: jobs packed into a few parts of the capital, two-and-a-half-hour commutes across the Valley of Mexico, and unpaid care work waiting at home after the paid shift.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum on Revolution Day: "They Will Fail Again"</u>

On the 116th anniversary of the Mexican Revolution, Sheinbaum warned those already working to delegitimize the 2027 elections that they will fail again. "They attack us because our honesty gets in their way. They know we will not submit. We are not decorative figures or instruments of the powerful." She compared it to the Porfiriato: railways and power plants built on concentrated power, rigged elections and dispossession. "Democracy does not end at the ballot box. The right to choose your rulers must come with the right to a dignified life."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>EU to Mexico: The Global Agreement Is Waiting on Your Senate</u>

Brussels has already approved it, so the next move belongs to Mexico's Senate. EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen told Mexican senators he expects progress on the Modernized Global Agreement before 2026 is out. He said Europe wants a relationship "of equals," not the "law of the strongest." First in line for wider European access: Mexican coffee, honey, cacao, avocado, mango, tequila and mezcal, while Washington keeps T-MEC hanging over Mexico's head.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>APEC Data: Mexico Out-Techs China, the US and Canada in Exports</u>

70.6% of Mexico's 2025 exports were medium- and high-tech manufactured goods. That puts Mexico 4th among all 21 APEC economies, ahead of China, the United States and Canada, according to APEC Policy Support Unit figures reported by El Economista.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Edomex 2027: Social Programs Up 7%, Zero New Debt, Zero New Taxes</u>

Governor Delfina Gómez sent a 433.8-billion-peso 2027 budget to the State of Mexico legislature: 231.3 billion, more than half, goes to social welfare, with an extra 1.4 billion for social programs (+7%) and 2.3 billion more for health. No new taxes, no tax hikes, the vehicle-tax subsidy stays, and for the fourth straight year the state takes on no new public debt. Mexico's most populous state spent decades under the PRI as a piggy bank for the Atlacomulco group.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Segob: Senior Pension Is a Constitutional Right, "Not for Some and Not for Others"</u>

After CEPAL and the World Bank credited Mexico's universal senior pension with cutting poverty and inequality, Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez pointed to who it reaches most: older women who spent their lives caring for children and grandchildren with no formal pension. "These are rights, they are in the Constitution, and they are not for some and not for others."

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Mexico and Cuba Restart Parliamentary Summit After Three-Year Freeze</u>

Mexico's Senate hosts the XVIII Mexico-Cuba Interparliamentary Meeting today and tomorrow, the first in three years. Senate president Higinio Martínez says health, economy, science, culture and sport are on the table, with a joint declaration expected. Cuban ambassador Eugenio Martínez Enríquez: "Mexico and Cuba are two sister countries, united."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Supreme Court Slams the Door on Grupo México: 18.4M Peso Fine Stands</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court threw out Buenavista del Cobre's last appeal against an 18.4-million-peso Profepa fine. Germán Larrea's Sonora copper mine was allowed 540,000 tons of mining waste and dumped 613,218 in 2022-23. Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar dismissed the appeal without even sending it to the full court: the case "does not hold exceptional legal interest." Same mine, same company that spilled 40,000 m³ of acidified copper sulfate into the Sonora River in 2014, poisoning 271 km of riverbed and 22,000 people.
